A scarlet geranium flowering hard in a cracked chimney pot that has been wedged in beside the tower's foot.
A single small shoe left on the leads where somebody kicked it off to climb better.
A dented tin mug hooked over the gallery rail by its handle, still steaming.
A jam jar of black tar with a brush standing up in it, wedged into the angle of the lattice.
A pigeon's nest built into the angle of the tower's ironwork with two eggs in it, the crew plainly working round it.
A cat's paw prints crossing the fresh snow on the leads and stopping dead at the parapet edge.
A child's carved wooden horse standing on the parapet cap, facing out over the city.
A rope hanging down the tower with a knot tied in it every foot, worn shiny where it is used as a measure.
A pot of white paint and a brush left on the gallery beside a fresh half-painted stripe that stops dead in the middle of a blade.
A sprig of holly with berries jammed into the lattice at head height.
A wooden crate wired to the tower's leg with straw in it and a speckled hen looking out of it.
One blade with an old mended crack running down it, bound across with three brass straps.
A cracked slate on the roof with a green fern growing out of the gap.
A kettle sitting on top of a hot vent pipe, genuinely boiling, with nobody near it.
A small mirror wired to the lattice at head height, angled so somebody can see behind themselves.
A washing rope strung from the tower's leg to a chimney with three odd socks pegged on it.
A sooty handprint left on the white band of the nearest blade.
A brass oil-can with a long curved spout standing upright and alone in the middle of the leads.
A bird's nest built right inside the bell of a disused vent cowl.
A dandelion in full flower growing out of a gutter that has silted up with soil.
A well-chewed rope end neatly whipped with twine to stop it going further.
Three spare blades leaned against the parapet, each painted a completely different colour.
A one-eyed seagull standing on the gallery rail with the air of owning the whole tower.
A rag knotted to a cable as a wind-telltale, standing straight out stiff.
A row of eleven little chalk-white pebbles set along the parapet cap in a line by somebody, for no reason anyone can see.
